subproblem.title: Allard scale at a point of density one (Simon 7.1, proof, first sentence)
subproblem.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, U an open subset of R^(n+l), V = v(M, theta) a rectifiable n-varifold in U (contract structure RectifiableVarifold n l U) with weight mu = mu_V, H : R^(n+l) -> R^(n+l), and p a real number with p > n, such that H is locally in L^p(mu) on U (integral over K of |H|^p dmu < infinity for every compact K contained in U). Let xi be in U with Theta^n(mu, xi) = 1, i.e. mu(B_r(xi)) / (omega_n r^n) -> 1 as r decreases to 0 (closed balls, quotient in [0, infinity]), and let delta > 0. Then xi is in spt V = U cap spt mu, and there is r > 0 with B_r(xi) contained in U, mu(B_r(xi)) <= (1 + delta) omega_n r^n and (r^(p-n) integral_{B_r(xi)} |H|^p dmu)^(1/p) <= delta (both inequalities in [0, infinity], the second being V.scaledLpNorm H p xi r <= delta).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ {n ℓ : ℕ} {U : Set (Amb n ℓ)} (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) (H : Amb n ℓ → Amb n ℓ) (p : ℝ) (ξ : Amb n ℓ) (δ : ℝ), IsOpen U → (n : ℝ) < p → V.LocallyLp H p → ξ ∈ U → V.HasDensity ξ 1 → 0 < δ → ξ ∈ V.support ∧ ∃ r : ℝ, 0 < r ∧ closedBall ξ r ⊆ U ∧ V.weight (closedBall ξ r) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal ((1 + δ) * (unitBallVolume n * r ^ n)) ∧ V.scaledLpNorm H p ξ r ≤ ENNReal.ofReal δ

Source: Simon, Ch. 5, proof of Theorem 7.1, first sentence (p. 127): 'Since lim_{rho->0} (rho^(p-n) int_{B_rho(xi)} |H|^p dmu_V)^(1/p) = 0 and lim_{rho->0} (omega_n rho^n)^(-1) mu_V(B_rho(xi)) = 1, we can choose rho > 0 such that the hypotheses of Theorem 5.2 hold'; this is step 1 of the parent proof with all details. Notation: mu = V.weight, omega_n = unitBallVolume n = pi^(n/2)/Gamma(n/2+1) > 0, balls B_r closed, all masses and integrals of nonnegative functions in [0, infinity].
1. Put m(r) := mu(B_r(xi)), v(r) := omega_n r^n in (0, infinity) for r > 0, and Q(r) := m(r)/v(r) in [0, infinity]. The hypothesis V.HasDensity xi 1 says exactly Q(r) -> 1 as r -> 0+.
2. xi is in spt mu. Let N be any neighbourhood of xi and choose e > 0 with B_e(xi) contained in N. Since Q(r) -> 1 > 0, the set of r in (0, e) with Q(r) > 0 is nonempty; for such r, m(r) > 0 (if m(r) = 0 then Q(r) = 0). Hence mu(N) >= m(r) > 0. As N was arbitrary, xi is in the support of mu, and since xi is in U, xi is in spt V = U cap spt mu.
3. Since U is open, choose r_0 > 0 with B_{r_0}(xi) contained in U. K := B_{r_0}(xi) is compact (closed and bounded in a finite-dimensional space) and contained in U, so A := integral_K |H|^p dmu < infinity by the local L^p hypothesis.
4. Mass bound for small r. Since Q(r) -> 1 < 1 + delta, there is r_1 in (0, r_0] such that Q(r) < 1 + delta for all r in (0, r_1). For such r, because v(r) is finite and positive, m(r) = Q(r) v(r) <= (1 + delta) v(r) = (1 + delta) omega_n r^n.
5. L^p bound for small r. For 0 < r <= r_0 we have B_r(xi) contained in K, so integral_{B_r(xi)} |H|^p dmu <= A, and therefore S(r) := (r^(p-n) integral_{B_r(xi)} |H|^p dmu)^(1/p) <= (r^(p-n) A)^(1/p), using that t -> t^(1/p) is nondecreasing on [0, infinity] (p > n >= 0, so 1/p > 0). As r -> 0+, r^(p-n) -> 0 because p - n > 0; since A < infinity, r^(p-n) A -> 0 in [0, infinity), and since t -> t^(1/p) is continuous at 0 with 0^(1/p) = 0, (r^(p-n) A)^(1/p) -> 0. As delta > 0, there is r_2 in (0, r_0] with S(r) <= delta for all r in (0, r_2).
6. Let r := min(r_1, r_2)/2 > 0. Then r <= r_0, so B_r(xi) is contained in B_{r_0}(xi), which is contained in U; r < r_1 gives mu(B_r(xi)) <= (1 + delta) omega_n r^n by step 4, and r < r_2 gives (r^(p-n) integral_{B_r(xi)} |H|^p dmu)^(1/p) <= delta by step 5. Together with step 2 this proves the claim.
proof_key_steps: Positive density at xi forces mu(N) > 0 for every neighbourhood N, so xi is in spt V
Fix a compact ball B_{r_0}(xi) in U; its |H|^p-integral A is finite
Mass ratio tends to 1 < 1 + delta, so the mass bound holds for small r
Scaled L^p norm is at most (r^(p-n) A)^(1/p), which tends to 0 since p > n
Take r below both thresholds and below r_0

subproblem.title: Carrier and support agree up to H^n-null sets when spt V has positive density (Simon 4.10(1), Ch. 1 3.6)
subproblem.statement: Let U be any subset of R^(n+l) and V = v(M, theta) a rectifiable n-varifold in U (contract structure) with weight mu. Suppose every xi in spt V = U cap spt mu has a positive density: there is a real t > 0 with mu(B_r(xi))/(omega_n r^n) -> t as r -> 0+ (V.HasDensity xi t). Then H^n(M symmetric-difference spt V) = 0, where H^n = muHE[n].
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ {n ℓ : ℕ} {U : Set (Amb n ℓ)} (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U), (∀ x ∈ V.support, ∃ t : ℝ, 0 < t ∧ V.HasDensity x t) → (μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)) (symmDiff V.carrier V.support) = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the parent proof ('carrier versus support', facts (F2) and (Leb)), which is the 'hence V = v(spt V cap U, Theta)' of Simon Ch. 4, Remark 4.10(1). The differentiation fact (Leb) is used in the form of Simon's Upper Density Theorem (Ch. 1, 3.6: if mu is Borel regular and A is mu-measurable with mu(A) < infinity, then Theta^{*n}(mu, A, x) := limsup_{rho->0} mu(A cap B_rho(x))/(omega_n rho^n) = 0 for H^n-a.e. x outside A), which needs no graph structure; this proves the conclusion of step 5 on all of spt V. Notation: mu = V.weight = theta H^n restricted to M (theta replaced by 0 off M); balls B_r closed, B'_r open. Simon's H^n and muHE[n] are both Hausdorff measures of dimension n, positive multiples of the unnormalized Hausdorff measure (in fact equal), so they have the same null sets. Simon's Ch. 1, Section 3 (Theorems 3.3-3.6) is stated for every real dimension n >= 0 (omega_0 = 1, H^0 = counting measure), so it applies for all n, including n = 0, which the statement allows.
1. Basic facts. (a) mu(R^(n+l) minus M) = 0, because mu is a density measure with respect to H^n restricted to M, and H^n restricted to M gives measure 0 to the complement of the null-measurable set M. (b) If A is an H^n-measurable subset of M with mu(A) = 0, then H^n(A) = 0: int_A theta dH^n = 0 and theta > 0 on A.
2. M minus spt V is H^n-null. Since spt V = U cap spt mu and M is contained in U, M minus spt V = M minus spt mu. Every point outside spt mu has an open neighbourhood of mu-measure 0 (definition of the support); R^(n+l) is second countable, so countably many of these cover the open set R^(n+l) minus spt mu, whence mu(R^(n+l) minus spt mu) = 0. The set A := M minus spt mu is H^n-measurable (M null-measurable, spt mu closed), contained in M, and mu(A) = 0, so H^n(A) = 0 by 1(b).
3. spt V minus M is H^n-null. Let N := spt V minus M. For x in N the hypothesis gives t_x in (0, infinity) with mu(B_r(x))/(omega_n r^n) -> t_x; in particular there is r_x > 0 with mu(B_{r_x}(x)) < infinity. The open balls B'_{r_x}(x), x in N, cover N, and by second countability (Lindelof) countably many of them, B'_j := B'_{r_j}(x_j), j = 1, 2, ..., cover N. Fix j and set A_j := M cap B_{r_j}(x_j). A_j is mu-measurable and mu(A_j) <= mu(B_{r_j}(x_j)) < infinity. mu is a Borel regular measure (a Borel measure on R^(n+l) whose outer measure has Borel hulls of equal measure), so the Upper Density Theorem gives an H^n-null set Z_j such that Theta^{*n}(mu, A_j, x) = 0 for every x outside A_j union Z_j. Let x be in N cap B'_j. Then x is not in M, so not in A_j; and for 0 < rho < r_j - |x - x_j| we have B_rho(x) contained in B_{r_j}(x_j), hence mu(A_j cap B_rho(x)) = mu(M cap B_rho(x)) = mu(B_rho(x)) by 1(a). Therefore Theta^{*n}(mu, A_j, x) = lim_{rho->0} mu(B_rho(x))/(omega_n rho^n) = t_x > 0, so x is in Z_j. Thus N cap B'_j is contained in Z_j and H^n(N) <= sum_j H^n(N cap B'_j) = 0.
4. Since M symmetric-difference spt V = (M minus spt V) union (spt V minus M), steps 2 and 3 give H^n(M symmetric-difference spt V) = 0.
proof_key_steps: mu vanishes off M, and mu-null subsets of M are H^n-null because theta > 0 on M
mu(complement of spt mu) = 0 by second countability, so M minus spt V is H^n-null
Positive finite density gives balls of finite mass around each point of spt V minus M; take a countable subcover
Upper Density Theorem for mu restricted to M cap ball: points of spt V minus M have positive density of M, so they form an H^n-null set

audit.reason: The stronger global conclusion is justified without openness of U. Positivity of multiplicity proves the carrier-minus-support direction. Positive finite density supplies finite-mass neighborhoods; the upper-density theorem and a countable subcover prove the reverse direction, including n = 0. Density is an explicit hypothesis, so no dependency on density_ge_one is required.

subproblem.title: Finite scaled C^{1,alpha} norm gives the Hoelder class C^{1,alpha}(W)
subproblem.statement: Let u : R^n -> R^l, B and W subsets of R^n with W contained in the interior of B, alpha > 0 and rho > 0. Suppose u is C^1 on B (ContDiffOn R 1 u B) and scaledC1AlphaNorm u B alpha rho = rho^{-1} sup_B |u| + sup_B |D_B u| + rho^alpha sup_{x != y in B} |D_B u(x) - D_B u(y)| / |x - y|^alpha < infinity (D_B u = derivative within B, |.| = Hilbert-Schmidt norm on linear maps, sums and suprema in [0, infinity]). Then IsHolderCkα 1 alpha u W: u is C^1 on W, there is a real Bd with ||iteratedFDeriv^i u(x)|| <= Bd for i in {0, 1} and x in W, and there is a real K with ||iteratedFDeriv^1 u(x) - iteratedFDeriv^1 u(y)|| <= K |x - y|^alpha for all x, y in W.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ {n ℓ : ℕ} (u : Rn n → Rn ℓ) (B W : Set (Rn n)) (α ρ : ℝ), 0 < α → 0 < ρ → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 u B → W ⊆ interior B → scaledC1AlphaNorm u B α ρ ≠ ∞ → IsHolderCkα 1 α u W
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof (the C^{1,1-n/p} class of u on W from the finite norm of Theorem 5.2), with all details.
1. Finiteness of the pieces. Write N := scaledC1AlphaNorm u B alpha rho = a S_0 + S_1 + b S_2 with a := rho^{-1} > 0, b := rho^alpha > 0, S_0 := sup_{x in B} |u(x)|, S_1 := sup_{x in B} |D_B u(x)|_HS, S_2 := sup_{x != y in B} |D_B u(x) - D_B u(y)|_HS / |x - y|^alpha, all in [0, infinity]. Since N < infinity, each summand is finite; as a and b are finite and positive, S_0, S_1, S_2 < infinity. Let s_0, s_1, s_2 >= 0 be their real values.
2. Derivatives on W. Let x be in W. Since W is contained in the interior of B, B is a neighbourhood of x; as u is C^1 on B, u is differentiable at x and D_B u(x) = Du(x) (the derivative within a neighbourhood of x is the derivative).
3. C^1 on W. W is contained in B, so u is C^1 on W (restriction of ContDiffOn to a subset).
4. Operator norm versus Hilbert-Schmidt norm. For a linear A : R^n -> R^l and v = sum_i v_i e_i: |A v| <= sum_i |v_i| |A e_i| <= (sum_i v_i^2)^(1/2) (sum_i |A e_i|^2)^(1/2) = |v| |A|_HS (Cauchy-Schwarz), hence ||A||_op <= |A|_HS.
5. Bounds of order 0 and 1. For x in W (contained in B): ||iteratedFDeriv^0 u(x)|| = |u(x)| <= s_0. The first iterated derivative is Du composed with the canonical linear isometry between linear maps and 1-multilinear maps, so ||iteratedFDeriv^1 u(x)|| = ||Du(x)||_op <= |Du(x)|_HS = |D_B u(x)|_HS <= s_1 (steps 2, 4). Now |(x, u(x))| = |z| < s, so |x| < s by step 1, i.e. x is in B'^n_s(0); thus x is in W and z = (x, u(x)) is in graph_W u.
5. graph_W u is contained in q^{-1}(S) cap B'_s(0). Let x be in W and z := (x, u(x)). Then |z| < s, so z is in B'_s(0). Also |x| < s, so z is in graph_{B^n_s(0)} u and q(z) is in q(graph_{B^n_s(0)} u); moreover |q(z)| = |z| < s, so q(z) is in q(graph_{B^n_s(0)} u) cap B_s(0) = S cap B_s(0). Thus q(z) is in S and z = q^{-1}(q(z)) is in q^{-1}(S).
6. Steps 2-5 show that W is open, contains 0, is contained in B'^n_s(0), and q^{-1}(S) cap B'_s(0) = graph_W u.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 3: Lemma 1.2 and Remark 1.3 (C^1 covering), proof of Theorem 1.6 'only if' with Remark 1.5(2),(3), Remark 1.8(1),(2) and Theorem 1.9 ('only if'), applied to the contract's varifold and localized to the open set U (theta is only assumed integrable on compact subsets of U). This is the input '(M) [Ch. 3 facts used in Ch. 4]' of the parent proof's fact (M). Notation: H^n = muHE[n] (H^n(lambda A + a) = lambda^n H^n(A) for lambda > 0, and H^n restricted to an n-dimensional subspace is n-dimensional Lebesgue measure on it, so H^n(P cap B_s(0)) = omega_n s^n); eta_{x,r}(y) = r^{-1}(y - x); mu = theta H^n restricted to M; balls B_r closed. For r > 0, x in R^(n+l), H^n-measurable A and h >= 0 or integrable, the change of variables y = eta_{x,r}(z) gives
(CV) int_{eta_{x,r}(A)} h(y) dH^n(y) = r^{-n} int_A h(eta_{x,r}(z)) dH^n(z).
Measurability convention. By the contract, theta is a.e.-measurable for H^n restricted to M, so there is a Borel function g with theta = g at H^n-a.e. point of M; fix a Borel H^n-null set Z' containing M cap {theta != g} (H^n is Borel regular); then also mu(Z') = 0. Since eta_{x,r} is a similarity (H^n(eta_{x,r}(S)) = r^{-n} H^n(S)), for f in C_c the function y -> f(y) theta(x + r y) agrees H^n-a.e. on eta_{x,r}(M) with the Borel function y -> f(y) g(x + r y). Hence the Bochner integrals in the definition of the approximate tangent space and in (CV) are integrals of a.e.-measurable functions, and they are finite (so not junk values) as soon as x + r spt f is contained in a compact subset of U, because theta is integrable on M cap K for every compact K contained in U.
1. C^1 covering (Lemma 1.2, Remark 1.3). By countable n-rectifiability, M is contained in Z_0 union U_j F_j(R^n) with H^n(Z_0) = 0 and F_j : R^n -> R^(n+l) Lipschitz. By the C^1 approximation theorem (Simon Ch. 2, Thm 1.5, applied to each coordinate function) there are, for each i, j, C^1 maps G_ij : R^n -> R^(n+l) with L^n({F_j != G_ij}) < 1/i. Then Z_j := R^n minus U_i {F_j = G_ij} is L^n-null, H^n(F_j(Z_j)) = 0 (Lipschitz images of L^n-null sets are H^n-null), and F_j(R^n) is contained in F_j(Z_j) union U_i G_ij(R^n). For a C^1 map G : R^n -> R^(n+l) let JG := (det(DG^T DG))^(1/2). By the area formula (Simon Ch. 2, Section 3) applied to the Lipschitz maps G restricted to {JG = 0} cap B_j(0), j = 1, 2, ..., we get H^n(G({JG = 0})) = 0. If JG(w_0) > 0, then DG(w_0) is injective with c_0 := min_{|e|=1} |DG(w_0) e| > 0; choosing an open ball B' around w_0 with ||DG(v) - DG(w_0)|| < c_0/2 on B' (continuity of DG) and with DG bounded on B', the mean value inequality gives |G(v) - G(v')| >= (c_0/2)|v - v'| for v, v' in B'. So G restricted to B' is a bi-Lipschitz C^1 embedding with injective derivative, a homeomorphism onto N := G(B'), and H^n(N) <= (sup_{B'} ||DG||)^n L^n(B') < infinity. By the Lindelof property countably many such balls cover the open set {JG > 0}. Collecting all G_ij and these balls, and replacing the union of the null sets by a Borel H^n-null superset N_0 (H^n is Borel regular), we get: M is contained in N_0 union U_{k>=1} N_k with H^n(N_0) = 0 and N_k = G_k(B'_k), G_k a C^1 map that is bi-Lipschitz on the open ball B'_k with injective derivative there, H^n(N_k) < infinity; each N_k is sigma-compact, hence Borel. Put M_0 := M cap N_0 and M_k := (M cap N_k) minus U_{0 <= i < k} N_i for k >= 1: the M_k are disjoint, H^n-measurable, M = U_{k>=0} M_k, H^n(M_0) = 0, M_k contained in N_k.
2. Blow-ups of N_k. For x = G_k(w) in N_k put T_x N_k := DG_k(w)(R^n), an n-dimensional subspace. Claim: for every f in C_c, lim_{r->0+} int_{eta_{x,r}(N_k)} f dH^n = int_{T_x N_k} f dH^n. By (CV) and the area formula for the injective Lipschitz map G_k on B'_k, int_{eta_{x,r}(N_k)} f dH^n = r^{-n} int_{B'_k} f((G_k(v) - x)/r) JG_k(v) dv = int_{(B'_k - w)/r} f((G_k(w + r s) - G_k(w))/r) JG_k(w + r s) ds. If spt f is in B_R(0), the integrand vanishes for |s| > 2R/c (bi-Lipschitz lower bound with constant c), is bounded by sup|f| sup_{B'_k} JG_k, and converges pointwise to f(DG_k(w) s) JG_k(w) (differentiability of G_k at w, continuity of f and JG_k). By dominated convergence the limit is int_{R^n} f(DG_k(w) s) JG_k(w) ds = int_{T_x N_k} f dH^n (area formula for the injective linear map DG_k(w)). Moreover x -> p_{T_x N_k} (orthogonal projection) is continuous on N_k: with A(w) := DG_k(w) injective, the projection onto its range is A (A^T A)^{-1} A^T, continuous in w, and w = G_k^{-1}(x) depends continuously on x in N_k.
3. Lusin decomposition (Remark 1.8(1)), localized to U. Since U is open, choose compact sets K_1, K_2, ... with K_m contained in the interior of K_{m+1} and U_m K_m = U. The measure mu_m := mu restricted to K_{m+1} (= theta H^n restricted to M cap K_{m+1}) is finite, because theta is integrable on M cap K_{m+1}. By Lusin's theorem (Simon Ch. 1, 1.17) for the finite Borel regular measure mu_m and the Borel function g (Measurability convention), for each i there is a closed set C_{m,i} contained in the measurable set (M cap K_m) minus Z' with mu(((M cap K_m) minus Z') minus C_{m,i}) < 1/i and g restricted to C_{m,i} continuous; since theta = g on M minus Z', theta restricted to C_{m,i} is continuous. C_{m,i} is compact, theta has a positive minimum c_{m,i} on it, so H^n(C_{m,i}) <= c_{m,i}^{-1} int_{C_{m,i}} theta dH^n < infinity. If A is an H^n-measurable subset of M with mu(A) = 0 then H^n(A) = 0 (int_A theta dH^n = 0 and theta > 0 on A); since (M cap K_m) minus U_i C_{m,i} is contained in Z' union (((M cap K_m) minus Z') minus U_i C_{m,i}), whose second part is a mu-null subset of M, we get H^n((M cap K_m) minus U_i C_{m,i}) = 0. Consequently M = Z union U_{m,i,k>=1} C_{m,i,k} with H^n(Z) = 0, where C_{m,i,k} := C_{m,i} cap M_k.
4. Tangent spaces at good points (proof of 1.6 'only if' and Remark 1.8(1)). Fix m, i, k >= 1 and C := C_{m,i,k}, an H^n-measurable subset of N_k cap M cap K_m with H^n(C) < infinity. By the Upper Density Theorem (Simon Ch. 1, 3.6) applied (i) to the finite Borel regular measure H^n restricted to N_k and the measurable set N_k minus C, and (ii) to the finite Borel regular measure mu_m and the set M minus C, there is an H^n-null set E = E_{m,i,k} such that for every x in C minus E: (E1) r^{-n} H^n((N_k minus C) cap B_r(x)) -> 0 and (E2) r^{-n} mu_m((M minus C) cap B_r(x)) -> 0 as r -> 0+. Fix x in C minus E and f in C_c with spt f in B_R(0); consider r so small that B_{rR}(x) is contained in the interior of K_{m+1} (possible since x is in K_m).
(4a) Unweighted blow-up. int_{eta_{x,r}(C)} f dH^n = int_{eta_{x,r}(N_k)} f dH^n - int_{eta_{x,r}(N_k minus C)} f dH^n. The first term tends to int_{T_x N_k} f dH^n (step 2); by (CV) the second is bounded by sup|f| r^{-n} H^n((N_k minus C) cap B_{rR}(x)) -> 0 (E1). Applying this to a continuous f with values in [0,1], f = 1 on B_1(0), spt f in B_2(0), we get limsup_{r->0} r^{-n} H^n(C cap B_r(x)) <= H^n(T_x N_k cap B_2(0)) = 2^n omega_n, so r^{-n} H^n(C cap B_{rR}(x)) stays bounded as r -> 0+ (Remark 1.5(3)).
(4b) Weighted blow-up. By (CV), int_{eta_{x,r}(M)} f(y) theta(x + r y) dH^n(y) = r^{-n} int_M f(eta_{x,r} z) theta(z) dH^n(z), which splits as r^{-n} int_{M minus C} f(eta_{x,r} z) theta(z) dH^n(z) + theta(x) int_{eta_{x,r}(C)} f dH^n + r^{-n} int_C f(eta_{x,r} z)(theta(z) - theta(x)) dH^n(z). The first part is bounded by sup|f| r^{-n} mu_m((M minus C) cap B_{rR}(x)) -> 0 (E2); the second tends to theta(x) int_{T_x N_k} f dH^n by (4a); the third is bounded by sup|f| sup{|theta(z) - theta(x)| : z in C cap B_{rR}(x)} r^{-n} H^n(C cap B_{rR}(x)) -> 0, by continuity of theta restricted to C at x and the boundedness in (4a). All integrals are finite, as the integrands vanish unless z is in B_{rR}(x), which is contained in K_{m+1}, where theta is integrable on M. Hence T_x N_k (of dimension n) is an approximate tangent space of M with respect to theta at x. With step 3, such a P exists at every x in M minus (Z union U_{m,i,k} E_{m,i,k}), i.e. at H^n-a.e. x in M.

Source: this is the translation step 'after applying the appropriate translation' of Simon's proof of 7.1 (p. 127) and fact (Inv) of the parent proof, proved in detail from the contract definitions. Notation: H^n = muHE[n]; mu = V.weight = (H^n restricted to M) with density ofReal(theta); tau(x) = x - xi with inverse tau^{-1}(x) = x + xi; for a set A, tau(A) = {a - xi : a in A} = (tau^{-1})^{-1}(A).
1. tau is a bijective isometry of R^(n+l), hence a homeomorphism and a measurable equivalence (Borel sets to Borel sets, both ways). Hausdorff measures, and hence H^n = muHE[n], are invariant under isometries: H^n(tau(A)) = H^n(A) for every A, tau_# H^n = H^n and (tau^{-1})_# H^n = H^n (tau is measure preserving for H^n).
2. Construction of V'. Put M' := tau(M) and theta'(x) := theta(x + xi). The structure fields hold: (a) M' is contained in tau(U) since M is contained in U. (b) M' = (tau^{-1})^{-1}(M) is H^n-null-measurable, because M is and preimages of null-measurable sets under the measure-preserving map tau^{-1} are null-measurable. (c) M' is countably n-rectifiable: if M is contained in M_0 union U_j F_j(R^n) with H^n(M_0) = 0 and F_j Lipschitz, then M' is contained in tau(M_0) union U_j (tau o F_j)(R^n), H^n(tau(M_0)) = H^n(M_0) = 0, and tau o F_j is Lipschitz with the same constant. (d) If x is in M' then x + xi is in M, so theta'(x) = theta(x + xi) > 0. (e) H^n restricted to M' equals tau_#(H^n restricted to M) (for Borel A: tau_#(H^n|M)(A) = H^n(tau^{-1}(A) cap M) = H^n(tau(tau^{-1}(A) cap M)) = H^n(A cap M')), and theta' o tau = theta; since a function f is a.e.-measurable for tau_# nu iff f o tau is a.e.-measurable for nu (tau a measurable equivalence), theta' is a.e.-measurable for H^n restricted to M'. (f) If K is compact and contained in tau(U), then K' := tau^{-1}(K) = K + xi is compact and contained in U, M' cap K = tau(M cap K'), and integrability (a.e. strong measurability together with finiteness of the integral) transfers as a whole under the measure-preserving equivalence tau: theta' is H^n-integrable on tau(M cap K') iff theta' o tau = theta is H^n-integrable on M cap K', which holds by hypothesis. So V' := v(M', theta') is a rectifiable n-varifold in tau(U), with carrier tau(M) and multiplicity theta(. + xi) by construction.
3. Weight. For Borel A: (tau_# mu)(A) = mu(tau^{-1}(A)) = int_{tau^{-1}(A)} ofReal(theta) d(H^n|M) = int_A ofReal(theta o tau^{-1}) d(tau_#(H^n|M)) = int_A ofReal(theta') d(H^n|M') = mu_{V'}(A), using the change of variables for the pushforward under the measurable equivalence tau and step 2(e). Hence mu_{V'} = tau_# mu.
4. Support. For a homeomorphism tau, spt(tau_# mu) = tau(spt mu): x is in spt(tau_# mu) iff every neighbourhood N of x has mu(tau^{-1}(N)) > 0 iff every neighbourhood of tau^{-1}(x) has positive mu-measure (tau^{-1} maps the neighbourhoods of x onto those of tau^{-1}(x)) iff tau^{-1}(x) is in spt mu. Therefore spt V' = tau(U) cap spt(mu_{V'}) = tau(U) cap tau(spt mu) = tau(U cap spt mu) = tau(spt V) (tau injective).
5. Tangent planes. For every x and every linear subspace P: P is an approximate tangent space of M' with respect to theta' at x (Simon Ch. 3, 1.7, i.e. HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' theta' x P) iff P is one of M with respect to theta at x + xi. 6. Divergence. For X in C^1 put Y := X o tau, i.e. Y(y) = X(y - xi). Then DY(y) = DX(tau y), so by step 5 div_M Y(y) = trace(DX(tau y) o tangentProj_V(y)) = trace(DX(tau y) o tangentProj_{V'}(tau y)) = div_{M'} X(tau y).
7. Proof of (i). Assume V has generalized mean curvature H in U. (a) Local integrability: let x be in tau(U), x = tau(y) with y in U. By hypothesis there is N, a neighbourhood of y within U, with int_N |H| dmu < infinity. Then tau(N) is a neighbourhood of x within tau(U) (tau homeomorphism) and, integrability transferring as a whole under the measurable equivalence tau, H' is (tau_# mu)-integrable on tau(N) iff H' o tau = H is mu-integrable on N, since H'(tau(y)) = H(y - xi + xi) = H(y). So H' is locally integrable on tau(U) for mu_{V'} = tau_# mu. (b) Let X be C^1 with compact support and tsupport X contained in tau(U). Then Y = X o tau is C^1, has compact support, and tsupport Y = tau^{-1}(tsupport X) is contained in U. The identity for V gives int div_M Y dmu = - int <Y, H> dmu. By the change of variables for pushforwards under the measurable equivalence tau (valid for Bochner integrals of arbitrary functions, integrable or not): int div_{M'} X dmu_{V'} = int (div_{M'} X) o tau dmu = int div_M Y dmu (step 6), and int <X, H'> dmu_{V'} = int <X(tau y), H'(tau y)> dmu(y) = int <Y, H> dmu. Hence int div_{M'} X dmu_{V'} = - int <X, H'> dmu_{V'}, i.e. V' has generalized mean curvature H' in tau(U).
8. Proof of (ii). Under the stated assumptions we check the seven parts of AllardHypotheses H' p delta r for V'. (a) 0 < r is assumed. (b) V' has generalized mean curvature H' in tau(U) by step 7. (c) theta' >= 1 mu_{V'}-a.e.: for the measurable equivalence tau, a property holds (tau_# mu)-a.e. iff its composition with tau holds mu-a.e.; and 1 <= theta'(tau y) = theta(y) holds for mu-a.e. y. (d) 0 = tau(xi) is in tau(spt V) = spt V' (step 4). (e) B_r(0) is contained in tau(U): if |z| <= r then z + xi is in B_r(xi), which is contained in U, and z = tau(z + xi). (f) mu_{V'}(B_r(0)) = mu(tau^{-1}(B_r(0))) = mu(B_r(xi)) <= (1 + delta) omega_n r^n, since tau^{-1}(B_r(0)) = {y : |y - xi| <= r} (closed balls are Borel). (g) int_{B_r(0)} |H'|^p dmu_{V'} = int_{tau^{-1}(B_r(0))} |H' o tau|^p dmu = int_{B_r(xi)} |H|^p dmu (change of variables for [0, infinity]-valued functions under a measurable equivalence; no measurability of H is needed), so (r^(p-n) int_{B_r(0)} |H'|^p dmu_{V'})^(1/p) = (r^(p-n) int_{B_r(xi)} |H|^p dmu)^(1/p) <= delta. Hence V'.AllardHypotheses H' p delta r. Steps 2-8 give all asserted properties of V'.

(G) for mu-a.e. x: P_x is an orthogonal projection of rank n and Theta^n(mu, x) = theta(x) >= 1.

(6.1) omega_n Theta^n(mu, xi) <= g(tau) <= exp((1/2) Lambda (tau/R)^(1-n/p)) tau^(-n) mu(B_tau(xi)) + (1/2) e^(Lambda/2) Lambda (tau/R)^(1-n/p).
